scope: STM32 application Core, USB/CAN, manual/autonomous/tuning integration; local offline only
record_kind: Summary transcribed from completed tool results; not a raw test log
raw_test_log_note: Test stdout was returned by the execution tool and was not redirected to a persistent log. Temporary test executables were removed by run_native.py on completion.

finding_fixed.problem: CHASSIS_TUNING_ENABLED and JETSON_AUTO_CHASSIS_TEST could both be enabled, scheduling two controllers for the same chassis.
finding_fixed.reproduction: Before the fix, preprocessing chassis_task.c with tuning=1, auto=0, chassis-test=1 succeeded and retained both Live_Tuning_Loop and Jetson_Auto_Loop.
finding_fixed.fix: Compile-time rejection of tuning combined with either autonomous mode.

normal_manual_firmware.note: ELF debug information changed; the complete flash binary remained byte-identical. No reflash is required for this guard.

review_conclusions: Manual timeout/revocation requires a new zero-velocity authorization before motion can resume.
Autonomous link timeout enters FAULT; restored coordinates or heartbeat do not automatically resume motion.
No other confirmed material defect was found in the reviewed state-machine, feedback, USB/CAN, numeric and wraparound interactions.
remaining_boundaries: Full autonomous mode remains unconfigured because the three physical travel distances are zero; the current default firmware is manual.
Offline HAL stubs and prior USB-disconnect tests do not establish motor autonomous stopping behavior after physical CAN disconnection or an MCU stall.
